title: Bubble and Squeak
subtitle: Crispy potato and cabbage patties
excerpt: Leftover mashed potato, cooked cabbage, and leek are mixed together and shaped into patties, then fried until the outside is golden and crispy. Bubble and squeak is a great way to use up vegetables from a roast dinner. Serve with a fried egg or cold meat.
sourceNotes: A British classic for using leftover vegetables. The name comes from the sounds the patties make as they fry.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Form the patties up to a day ahead. Store on a plate in the fridge until ready to fry.

content.text: Press the patties firmly before frying so they hold together. Cold leftover mash works better than freshly made as it is drier and binds more easily.

items.prepNote: finely diced and softened in butter

content.text: Cook the onion in half the butter over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft. Set aside to cool.
Put the mashed potato, cabbage, leek, and cooked onion in a bowl. Mix well. Season generously with salt.
Add the beaten egg. Mix until the mixture holds together.
Divide into 8 portions. Shape each into a flat patty about 2cm thick.
Dust each patty lightly in plain flour on both sides.
Heat the remaining butter in a frying pan over medium heat. When foaming, add 4 patties. Cook for 4 minutes each side until deep golden. Cook in two batches.

items.symptom: Patties are falling apart in the pan
items.cause: Mix is too wet or not enough egg
items.fix: Add more flour to the mix and chill before frying.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too much butter pooling
items.fix: Increase heat to medium-high and use less butter.
Flatten to 1.5cm and cook 1 minute longer each side.
